catalog_quote: Nouns and adjectives are stressed on the last non-enclitic syllable. Verbs are normally stressed on the endings, or, in the absence of endings, on the stem. Progressive tenses are stressed on the last syllable of the infinitive (or past stem, see § 3.4). The negative verbal prefixes, ne- and na- (see also § 3.5), generally shift stress away from final position: e.g. rowt-óm ‘I went’, ne-rówt-om ‘I did not go’.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (43 pp., text, the PDF's metadata). PDF page 6 = printed p. 150 carries the heading "2.3 Stress" and the passage exactly as quoted (only line-break hyphenations "nor-mally", "Pro-gressive" differ): "Nouns and adjectives are stressed on the last non-enclitic syllable. Verbs are normally stressed on the endings, or, in the absence of endings, on the stem. Progressive tenses are stressed on the last syllable of the infinitive (or past stem, see § 3.4). The negative verbal prefixes, ne- and na- (see also § 3.5), generally shift stress away from final position: e.g. rowt-óm 'I went', ne-rówt-om 'I did not go'." Page 1 of the PDF states "© 2023 The Author(s). This is an Open Access article…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Persian-type final stress: nominals carry stress on the last syllable of the word excluding enclitics; verbs are stressed on the (final) personal ending, or on the stem if there is none, except that negative/prohibitive/subjunctive prefixes take the stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Negative verbal prefixes ne-/na- (and per Korn 2022 the prohibitive ma- and the stressed irrealis/subjunctive prefix be-) attract stress away from the final syllable: rowt-óm 'I went' vs ne-rówt-om 'I did not go'. Progressive tenses stress the last syllable of the infinitive/past stem; the progressive prefix be- is unstressed (Korn 2022 handout).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (nouns, adjectives, verbs), stated for the South Bashkardi (Molkigal) sub-dialect of Garu village, based on one narrated folktale plus the author's 2008 ELDP fieldwork. Enclitics (=e EZ, =ō indefinite, possessive =ī, directional -å per Korn 2017) are outside the stress domain. Corroborated for the 1956 Gershevitch corpus (North and South Bashkardi) by Korn 2017 §3.3: 'like in Persian, nominals are stressed on the last syllable of the stem in Bashkardi'.
new_statements.identity_note: The deciding statement describes the South Bashkardi (Molkigal) sub-dialect of Garu village, a South Bashkardi island near Minab; Glottolog dialect sout2644 'Southern Bashaka' (child of bash1263). Korn 2017's final-stem-stress remark covers both North and South Bashkardi from Gershevitch's 1956 recordings, so the rule appears to hold across bash1263. Glottolog also files Bandari, Minabi and Rudani sources under bash1263; those varieties were not covered by any stress statement found (Iranica BANDARI is silent).
